headline: Rain and floods send fish and vegetable prices soaring in Dhaka
summary: Heavy rainfall and flooding have disrupted supply chains, leading to a sharp increase in the cost of essential food items in the capital.
details: Heavy rain and floods have caused a significant spike in the fish and vegetable prices across Dhaka city.
The adverse weather conditions have disrupted the transportation of produce from rural areas to the capital's markets.
Supplies of fresh vegetables and fish have dwindled, leading to higher costs for consumers.
Market vendors report that the shortage of supply is the primary driver behind the price hike.
Residents of Dhaka are facing increased daily expenses as essential food items become more expensive.
The situation is expected to continue as long as the flood-affected regions struggle to recover and restore supply lines.
caption:
Essential food prices are spiking in Dhaka as rain and floods disrupt supply chains.

Heavy rain and floods have caused a significant spike in the fish and vegetable prices across Dhaka city.

The adverse weather conditions have disrupted the transportation of produce from rural areas to the capital's markets.

Supplies of fresh vegetables and fish have dwindled, leading to higher costs for consumers.

Market vendors report that the shortage of supply is the primary driver behind the price hike.

Residents of Dhaka are facing increased daily expenses as essential food items become more expensive.

The situation is expected to continue as long as the flood-affected regions struggle to recover and restore supply lines.

headline_marked: 27 members of notorious Chhoto Jahangir gang [[surrender in the Sundarbans]]
headline: 27 members of notorious Chhoto Jahangir gang surrender in the Sundarbans
summary: The gang leader and 26 associates handed over a large cache of firearms and ammunition to the Bangladesh Coast Guard.
details: The leader of the notorious Chhoto Jahangir gang, Jahangir Sheikh (45), and 26 of his associates surrendered to the Bangladesh Coast Guard in the Sundarbans yesterday.
The surrender took place around 5:00 PM near Charputia canal under Mongla Police Station in Bagerhat, according to a Coast Guard statement.

The group handed over a significant cache of weapons, including three foreign firearms, one eight-shooter, one four-shooter, five locally made single-barrel guns, 15 locally made pipe guns, and two Chinese pipe guns.
Along with the weapons, they surrendered 340 rounds of live ammunition and 55 spent cartridges.
The Coast Guard stated that the gang had long been involved in robberies within the Sundarbans and the abduction of fishermen and bawalis for ransom.

The surrendering members hail from various regions, including Dacope, Koyra, and Batiaghata in Khulna, as well as Rampal, Fakirhat, Kachua, Morrelganj, and Sarankhola in Bagerhat, and Mathbaria in Pirojpur.
This follows previous surrenders of seven members from the Chhoto Suman gang and three active members of the Boro Jahangir gang, who also handed over arms and ammunition.
caption:

The leader of the notorious Chhoto Jahangir gang, Jahangir Sheikh (45), and 26 of his associates surrendered to the Bangladesh Coast Guard in the Sundarbans yesterday.

The surrender took place around 5:00 PM near Charputia canal under Mongla Police Station in Bagerhat, according to a Coast Guard statement.

The group handed over a significant cache of weapons, including three foreign firearms, one eight-shooter, one four-shooter, five locally made single-barrel guns, 15 locally made pipe guns, and two Chinese pipe guns.

Along with the weapons, they surrendered 340 rounds of live ammunition and 55 spent cartridges.

The Coast Guard stated that the gang had long been involved in robberies within the Sundarbans and the abduction of fishermen and bawalis for ransom.

The surrendering members hail from various regions, including Dacope, Koyra, and Batiaghata in Khulna, as well as Rampal, Fakirhat, Kachua, Morrelganj, and Sarankhola in Bagerhat, and Mathbaria in Pirojpur.

This follows previous surrenders of seven members from the Chhoto Suman gang and three active members of the Boro Jahangir gang, who also handed over arms and ammunition.
